title: A multiphysics computational framework for evaluating ATP response and thermal loading during skeletal muscle photobiomodulation
task: Evaluate ATP response and thermal effects during photobiomodulation across tissue layers
key_results: At 850 nm with 0.75 W optical power, muscle ATP response plateaus at ~14.73% while maximum temperature reaches 38.584°C; higher power (2.50 W) increases thermal loading to 45.857°C with diminished ATP response (~12.29%)
comments: The phenomenological ATP model is acknowledged as conditional on tissue properties and parameters; experimental validation is essential before clinical translation.

model_io.model: 3D multiphysics framework (light transport + heat transfer + ATP dynamics)
outputs: light penetration depth and intensity in muscle

hypotheses.hypothesis: Longer wavelengths (900 nm) penetrate deeper muscle than shorter wavelengths
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 900 nm produces highest average and maximum light in muscle

hypotheses.hypothesis: Greater optical power monotonically increases ATP response
hypotheses.result: Refuted: ATP response peaks at 0.50-0.75 W then decreases, while thermal loading increases continuously

title: Differential interactions of curcumin with POPC/cholesterol and POPS/cholesterol mixed monolayers at air-water interface
task: Characterize differential curcumin interactions with neutral vs. charged lipid monolayers
key_results: Curcumin binds significantly stronger to POPS/Chol monolayers than POPC/Chol; forms aggregates in POPC/Chol but not POPS/Chol films; interaction mechanism involves ion-dipole interactions with negatively charged PS head groups
comments: The aggregate formation difference suggests electrostatic complementarity drives selective membrane binding, with potential implications for anticancer selectivity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Charged PS head groups interact more strongly with curcumin than neutral PC groups
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: POPS/Chol shows greater interaction strength and different response pattern than POPC/Chol

hypotheses.hypothesis: Curcumin aggregation state differs between neutral and charged monolayers
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: aggregates observed in POPC/Chol but not POPS/Chol

title: AP2M1 promotes TNBC progression by stabilizing EGFR through inhibition of lysosomal degradation
task: Elucidating the mechanism by which AP2M1 stabilizes EGFR and promotes TNBC progression
key_results: AP2M1 upregulated 3-5 fold in TNBC tissues; AP2M1 silencing accelerates EGFR internalization and lysosomal degradation; high AP2M1 correlates with poor prognosis

model_io.model: TNBC cell lines and xenografts; transcriptome analysis of paired tissues

hypotheses.hypothesis: AP2M1 stabilizes EGFR by inhibiting its lysosomal degradation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; AP2M1 silencing promotes EGFR ubiquitination and degradation

title: ATF6 shapes PERK and IRE1 signaling dynamics during ER stress
task: Characterizing ATF6's role in modulating PERK and IRE1 signaling during ER stress
key_results: ATF6 promotes PERK expression during early stress and dampens IRE1 RNase activity during prolonged stress; ATF6 loss leads to prolonged IRE1 signaling

hypotheses.hypothesis: ATF6 signaling intersects with PERK and IRE1 branches to fine-tune UPR responses
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ATF6 regulates temporal dynamics of both pathways

title: Insights into cardiovascular development of zebrafish embryo after exposure to dolutegravir

title: Linking centromere stretch to SAC signaling in mammalian oocytes with insights from modified kinetochore model
task: Determining whether centromere stretching is required for spindle assembly checkpoint silencing in mammalian oocytes
key_results: Modified kinetochores with stable microtubule attachments but no centromere stretching show persistent SAC signaling; centromere stretching correlates strongly with SAC deactivation; impaired oscillatory movements observed
comments: The finding that attachment alone is insufficient challenges the mitotic paradigm and suggests meiotic SAC regulation depends on a distinct mechanical signal.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Centromere stretching correlates with SAC signaling in oocytes
